rationale: talkSPORT (Aug 3): Spurs are open to selling, and West Ham (relegated to the Championship) want him; football.london (Aug 4) says West Ham have already held talks and promoted Hull City are also interested. Fiorentina refused the GBP8.5m option and are unlikely to return because they are closing on a Mastantuono loan. His agent wants a permanent move and prefers a top-five league, which favours Hull.

Conditional on a move, PSG are still the only named suitor: SPORT (via HT, Aug 1) says PSG intensified their pursuit with a five-year contract offer, though there is no club-to-club deal yet. On Aug 4 (AFP) Torres said 'in football you never know... waiting to make the right decision', and Flick said Barca's striker plans 'depend on Ferran'.

Di Marzio (via football.london, Jul 28) says Inter are the club that asked about Spence, but Spurs raised the price from about EUR30m to over EUR40m. He doubts Inter will pay that and says De Zerbi is unsure about selling, so a move is less likely, though Inter remain the clear lead conditional on one. Spurs are said to be open to offers (Jul 28).

No concrete progress since Jul 24. Express & Star (Jul 31) repeats Fenerbahce's earlier GBP30m interest and Man Utd links, and Villa's Jackson pursuit, which would open the door to a Watkins sale, is still not agreed (Plettenberg, Jul 27). Fenerbahce reportedly have personal terms, but Villa rejected GBP30-35m.

Estadio Deportivo (Aug 2, low reliability) claims Arsenal bid EUR75m, and CaughtOffside (via Sports Mole, Aug 2) says Konsa is open to Arsenal while Villa want at least GBP60m. Liverpool are raised because the Guardian (Aug 3) says they lack experienced centre-backs after Konate left and Gomez was injured, and fan-site reports name Konsa as a target. Arsenal's budget is also being spent on Bruno Guimaraes (GBP70m bid rejected, Aug 3).

The deal has revived: The Times (Jul 28) says Spurs are working on a GBP60m deal, and BBC/Sami Mokbel (Jul 28-29) says Savinho is keen to leave this window to join Spurs, with 'machinations... under way' and City aware. There is no club-to-club agreement yet, and AC Milan are reportedly monitoring.

The Athletic/Ornstein (Jul 31, via africasoccer Aug 1) says Man Utd reached agreement with Brighton for GBP75m fixed plus up to GBP7m in add-ons, with permission for a medical and the player pushing for the move. Official completion had not been seen as of Aug 4.

No new Marmoush news since Jul 9, when Atletico were the leading target and City were open to a sale at about EUR60m. Juventus are cut because they signed Kolo Muani (EUR38m) and Alajbegovic on Aug 2. Spurs are still short of forwards (football.london, Aug 4).

He is still a free agent (Sofascore, Aug 4). Goal (Jul 21) says Al-Ittihad are negotiating a one-year renewal, which would not count as a new club, that Cruzeiro and Palmeiras are keen, and that Fabinho prioritises European and Saudi clubs. Sevilla (Fichajes, Jul 5) and Fenerbahce are earlier links.

Plettenberg/Sky (Aug 3) says Bouaddi has a 'full verbal agreement' with City to 2031 and City are in pole position, with the fee still open (about EUR90m guaranteed vs Lille's roughly EUR100m), and TEAMtalk (Aug 4) reports growing confidence. Lille's president (Jul 31) denied any agreement and expects him to stay, and other clubs, including Liverpool, are monitoring.
UNCHANGED: no Hadjam transfer reports were found from Jul 1 to Aug 4 in either search or the archive. He was benched for Algeria's World Cup last-32 exit (Jul 3).

Palmeiras rejected Aston Villa's EUR25m+5m bid (ge/ESPN, Jul 28-29) and say Allan is not for sale, though EUR45m might change that (ESPN Brasil, Jul 29). Newcastle, Liverpool, Zenit and Napoli (an earlier EUR35m approach) are other reported suitors, but Villa are the latest active bidder as they replace Rogers.

Plettenberg (Jul 27): Villa are in direct talks with Chelsea and Jackson's camp about a permanent move or a loan, with no agreement yet. A low-quality report (Aug 1) claims a deal is agreed, and Chelsea signing Welbeck (Aug 1) makes Jackson more expendable. Juventus are cut after signing Kolo Muani, and the risk remains that a loan structure would not count.

Conditional on a move, Real Madrid are still the only real destination, but Yahoo (Jul 26) notes Real's budget and midfield slot are contested by their Rodri pursuit and Diomande spending (EUR120m). His role under Alonso is unclear after Rogers' arrival, and no new Real-Enzo talks were reported.

Romano (Aug 3): Liverpool and PSG are in official club-to-club talks after an initial offer of over EUR100m, far from PSG's EUR170m ask. Barcola 'loves the idea' of Liverpool, personal terms are not an issue, and PSG are lining up replacements (Godts bid, Akliouche). Arsenal are focused on Vinicius and Bruno Guimaraes.

Romano (Aug 2): Juventus formally told Villa they are ending the pursuit because 'costs of the deal are too high', and Juve and PSG are now in talks with Parma for Suzuki (Romano, Jul 27). Villa insist he stays. Juve remain the most likely destination only if the deal is revived, and no other suitor is named.

The Mirror/Calciomercato (Jul 22) say Arsenal will sell for about GBP38-43m and that Man Utd, Newcastle and Bayern are keeping tabs. Newcastle are raised because they need wingers after selling Gordon, while Juventus (who signed winger Alajbegovic on Aug 2) and PSG (signing Godts and Akliouche) are cut. No bid has been reported.

The latest reports are still Jul 22: the Athletic says Arsenal value him at GBP18-20m with AC Milan interested, and Calciomercato says a deal near GBP16m could be finalised. He was still playing for Arsenal on Aug 1 (scored vs Girona), his GBP265k/week wage is a hurdle, and Juventus are cut after signing Kolo Muani.

Conditional on a move: The Athletic (via HT, Jul 26) says Real are actively working on a deal, are increasingly confident and are offering a contract to 2030, though formal talks had not started. Rodri had minor back surgery on Jul 28, and Maresca (Jul 31) called the links 'speculation', so a move by Aug 6 is unlikely, but Real are dominant if one happens.
